summary: The exact candidate fixes speculative decode-stage classification and removes synchronous torch trace export from both legacy and profile-v2 scheduler stop paths. Independent tests also confirm that export threads no longer use the scheduler process group, eliminating the reviewed collective-ordering hang.

tests.what_was_measured: On the prepared base, TARGET_VERIFY was classified as prefill rather than decode.
On the prepared base, legacy stop remained inside the mocked exporter for its five-second timeout.
On the prepared base, profile-v2 stop remained inside the mocked exporter for its five-second timeout.
At the candidate commit, five tests passed, including speculative classification and nonblocking/no-barrier behavior for legacy and profile-v2 paths.
At the candidate commit, two staggered Gloo ranks completed a normal all-reduce with value 3.0 while trace exports ran.
Thirteen existing profile merge and API tests passed at the candidate commit.
Legacy stop returned before export completion on gfx950, then produced a 41810-byte trace; GPU matmul max absolute error was 2.86102294921875e-05.
Profile-v2 stop returned before export completion on gfx950, then produced a 41668-byte trace; GPU matmul max absolute error was 2.6702880859375e-05.

gpu_execution.evidence: Both profiler implementations generated nonempty traces around a real 256x256 matrix multiplication on AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950.

remaining_limitations: Only one AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 GPU was available; no B200 x8 or multi-rank GPU profile was run.
GLM-5.2 weights and the TP8/MTP serving workload were unavailable, so the reported 25-second duration and end-to-end TTFT delta were not reproduced.
The distributed ordering test used two Gloo CPU ranks.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
